### Changes
- **Own Modbus connection** (pymodbus) instead of the shared Home Assistant one. One client per unit, all reads and writes serialized behind a lock, timeout 3 s, one retry. The unit is expected directly on port 502 (no proxy needed).
- **Reconnects by itself**: a dead connection is closed and rebuilt; after a failure the next attempt waits 5, 15, 30, then 60 s instead of retrying on every poll.
- **Fewer requests**: the 12 register blocks are read with 5 requests (merged, with fallback to the single blocks if the unit rejects a merged one). Default update interval stays 30 s, the option now allows 10–300 s.
- **No error floods**: a failed poll stops at the first error and keeps the last values. Entities become unavailable after 3 failed polls in a row. One warning when the unit stops answering, one message when it is back.
- **Throttled bus writes**: at most one write per input every 30 s, only while connected. CO₂ (register 764) is written when it moved by 25 ppm or more, or after 5 minutes. A failed write is not queued.
- **Less state churn**: an entity only writes a new state when one of its registers changed.

### Requirements
- No longer needs Home Assistant's `modbus` integration or Home Assistant 2026.9; needs `pymodbus` (installed automatically).

Entities and configuration are unchanged; updating from 0.2.x needs no action. If the unit was reached through a proxy on another port, set host and port via **Reconfigure**.
